clue.text: I would feel bitter about a lodger

indicators.note: about means one word wraps round the other here, the bitterness surrounding the I would

parts.note: to feel bitter is to resent
I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone resents the person renting their spare room.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in a house, as a paying lodger does, is one of its inhabitants.

clue.text: I fall for this attempt at self-advertisement

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I
to trip is to stumble or fall

explanation.surface: A confession of being taken in by someone's bid for publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A vanity exercise undertaken mainly to boost one's own image or importance.

clue.text: Lying parson

explanation.surface: A clergyman telling untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying down (recumbent, resting on something) is one sense; the holder of a church benefice is the other.

clue.text: One or other number has a one in it

indicators.note: in it says the one is placed inside the number

parts.note: a number here is something that numbs, an anaesthetic such as ether
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a figure containing the digit one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as 'numb-er', a thing that numbs: ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: The word picks out one of two alternatives, whichever.

clue.text: List of affirmative votes, perhaps, showing the subject matter

explanation.surface: A tally of yes votes revealing what a debate was about.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Lords peers vote 'Content' or 'Not content', so a table of Contents could list the yes votes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabulation of those voting yes in the Lords, and the page at the front of a book listing its chapters and topics.

clue.text: Companies holding English classes

indicators.note: holding means the companies surround the English abbreviation

parts.note: casts are companies of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Firms run English lessons for staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary social ranks, as in the Hindu system, are social classes.

clue.text: Having no responsibility for vehicle bearing getting loose

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
E, east, is a compass bearing
loose means free, unrestrained

explanation.surface: Someone not liable when a car's bearing comes loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks mechanical, as in a wheel bearing, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Untroubled and without duties or worries.

clue.text: Note about fur-manufacturer's de-tailed ends of lines

indicators.note: about means the musical note goes round the shortened animal

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: de-tailed means the final letter is docked from the animal's name

parts.note: the ermine, a stoat in winter coat, produces a prized white fur

explanation.surface: A musical note on a furrier's detailed records.
explanation.walkthrough: The ermine is the stoat in its white winter coat, so it 'manufactures' the fur; 'de-tailed' docks its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway or bus stations at the far end of a route are terminal points.

clue.text: Incidental information on this gelid compound

indicators.note: compound means the letters are mixed together into something new

explanation.surface: A side note on a frozen chemical compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a chemistry noun but signals rearranging THIS GELID.
explanation.definitionFit: A side remark or fact that throws unexpected light on a subject.

clue.text: This animal is heard in U.S. links

definitions.text: This animal is heard in U.S. links

parts.words: This animal is heard in U.S. links
parts.note: the word links sounds like lynx, and the animal sought is the North American species of lynx

explanation.surface: Some creature can be heard on American golf courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' suggests a golf course; said aloud it is 'lynx', and the American lynx is the one sought.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-tailed wild cat of North America, a close relative of the lynx.

clue.text: Haggled over terms, like Marenka

explanation.surface: Someone bargained like a character from an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Marenka is the heroine of Smetana's opera The Bartered Bride.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanged goods by trading and bargaining; and sold off in marriage, as the bride in Smetana's opera is.

clue.text: First performance in Eden, say-and Eve's last!

parts.note: Anthony Eden was a British prime minister, a premier

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of Eve's

explanation.surface: A scene from Genesis: a debut staged in the Garden of Eden, with Eve having the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden looks like the biblical garden but is the 1950s Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening night of a play or film, its debut showing.

clue.text: Terminal receives one finishing touch to the roof

indicators.note: receives means the terminal word takes the one inside it

parts.note: terminal means final, at the end
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An airport terminal is given its last roofing detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' looks like an airport building but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament on the top of a gable or spire, crowning the roof.

clue.text: Noticed shop-front of various colours

indicators.note: front picks the opening letter of shop

parts.note: pied means patchily coloured, as a magpie is

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a brightly painted shopfront.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught sight of, observed.

clue.text: Liable to be preoccupied, old boy bows out of court sittings

indicators.note: bows out means the old boy leaves the longer word

parts.note: obsessional means prone to fixations

explanation.surface: An obsessive former pupil withdraws from a series of court hearings.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the periods during which a court or legislature sits.

clue.text: Making a pretence of moving

explanation.surface: Someone faking emotion in a touching way.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on or feigning something; and stirring the emotions, touching.

clue.text: Most of the writers' supplies needed for a study group

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: ink is a writer's supply
a tank is a reservoir holding a supply, here of ink

explanation.surface: Stationery requirements for a group of scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' applies to 'the' alone; a writer once kept ink in a tank or well, so both are writers' supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of experts gathered to research and generate ideas on policy.

clue.text: Takes for granted afterthought about summary

indicators.note: about means the afterthought wraps round the summary

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an afterthought in a letter
a résumé is a summary

explanation.surface: A note added to a letter on top of a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumes without proof.

clue.text: Private cabin, say, has space

parts.note: to say is to state
room means space

explanation.surface: A ship's private cabin is said to be roomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A private sleeping compartment on a ship or train.

clue.text: English in Madrid not exactly looked up to

indicators.note: in means the English abbreviation goes into Madrid
not exactly means the letters are not in their exact order

explanation.surface: An Englishman in Madrid is not quite respected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside MADRID; 'not exactly' rearranges the resulting letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Regarded with respect and approval.

clue.text: The old man of the island?

definitions.text: The old man of the island?

parts.words: The old man of the island?
parts.note: an old word for a person or creature also names an island off England's south coast

explanation.surface: A question about some elderly islander.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is off the south coast of England; 'wight' is also an archaic word for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a human being, matching the Isle of that name.

clue.text: One who'd cut loose in a dance

definitions.text: One who'd cut loose in a dance

parts.words: One who'd cut loose in a dance
parts.note: a garden tool that cuts weeds, letting rip, suggests a lively country dance; one who'd cut is one who hoed

explanation.surface: Someone letting their hair down at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoe cuts weeds; read as a hoe going 'down' loose, it gives the American barn dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively American folk dance or social gathering for such dancing.

clue.text: There's gold in the air in the early morning

indicators.note: in means the gold sits inside the air

parts.note: an aura is an air or atmosphere about something
or is heraldic gold

explanation.surface: Dawn light gilds the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Aurora was the Roman goddess of the dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn, from the Roman goddess of daybreak.

clue.text: Get a foot in the early morning transport

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held and on the scan, 'Get a foot in the early morning transport', has AM and BUS but no word giving the opening I of IAMBUS
annotationWithheld.clue: Get a foot in the early morning transport

clue.text: Bed right for one who bends his knee

parts.note: a truckle is a low bed on wheels stored under another

explanation.surface: A bed suitable for someone who kneels.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who submits obsequiously, a toady.

clue.text: A Scandinavian has no right to reject titles

indicators.note: reject means the titles are thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: titles are names

explanation.surface: A Swede or Dane is not entitled to turn down honours.
explanation.definitionFit: A Viking or ancient inhabitant of Scandinavia.

clue.text: He addresses the troops taking a hill

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are troops who are not officers
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: An officer delivers a speech to soldiers storming a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A public speaker, one who gives speeches.

clue.text: They may be given toast at dinner

definitions.text: They may be given toast at dinner

parts.words: They may be given toast at dinner
parts.note: reads like guests served bread, but refers to the formal toast drunk to the women present at a dinner

explanation.surface: Diners being served toasted bread.
explanation.walkthrough: At formal British dinners a toast is traditionally proposed to 'the Ladies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Women, honoured in a customary after-dinner toast.

clue.text: Excellent bridge authority

parts.note: a span is a bridge or its arch
a king is a ruling authority

explanation.surface: A top bridge player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game but is a structure spanning a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, splendid or first-rate, as in a spanking new car.
